questions.q: In "Know your customer and market Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Hold a ten-minute team check each day: yesterday's problem, today's plan, one risk.
Choose three measures: speed, quality (errors per 100) and customer rating. Review them every week.
Create two options at most, so choice stays easy.
Choose one first segment and say why the others wait.

questions.q: In "Rules, registration and data duties in Brazil Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Learn the tax regime that fits your size and write down which taxes you will collect and pay, and when.
Interview at least eight real customers with open questions. Record exact words, not your summary.
Set one measurable target for 90 days, such as 'raise repeat customers from 20% to 30%'.
Keep an incident and near-miss log. Near-misses are free lessons.

questions.q: In "Design the offer Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Add one proof for each promise: a sample, a test result, a guarantee or a customer record.
Test the plan: what if sales fall by a quarter, or cost rises by a tenth?
In sports: Train coaches in safeguarding children and basic life support.
Review monthly: numbers, defects, complaints, cash. Write three decisions each time.

questions.q: In "Run the work step by step Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Set service rules for answering customers: reply times, tone, how to apologise and fix.
Count the market in units: how many sessions could one area buy in a month? Use two public sources and your own count, then take the lower figure.
Choose three measures: speed, quality (errors per 100) and customer rating. Review them every week.
Keep money for business and money for the owner apart.

questions.q: In "Safety, quality and risk Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: In sports: Grow through community events and visible player progress.
Describe the core offer in three lines: what is delivered (a coaching, event or facility service), the standard it meets, and the time it takes.
Map the process from first contact to paid and closed. Typical stages: enquiry, quote, preparation, delivery of the session, check, payment, follow-up.
In sports: Injury risk from overload; set age-appropriate load and rest.

questions.q: In "People, skills and service Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Name the key resource at each stage: a safe space and a qualified coach. Note what happens if it is missing.
Train by showing, doing with support, then doing alone with a check. Record sign-off per task.
Write the customer in one sentence: a player, club or school. Add the place, the moment of need and what they use today.
List ten things that could go wrong. Score each for how likely (1 to 5) and how serious (1 to 5). Multiply and sort.

questions.q: In "Money: cost, price and break-even Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Ask each customer how they found you, and record it. Spend more where the record shows results.
Build a growth path: what a new person can do in week 1, month 3 and month 12.
Break-even units = fixed cost divided by contribution. Plan to pass it by a safe margin.
Name the key resource at each stage: a safe space and a qualified coach. Note what happens if it is missing.

questions.q: In "Grow, measure and renew Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Find the sector rules for sports: licences, inspections, professional registers. List each with the office that issues it and the renewal date.
Review monthly: numbers, defects, complaints, cash. Write three decisions each time.
Personal data of customers falls under Brazil's data protection law (LGPD). Collect only what you need, say why, keep it safe, and name who answers questions.
Map the process from first contact to paid and closed. Typical stages: enquiry, quote, preparation, delivery of the session, check, payment, follow-up.
